      {
        "@type": "Question",
        "name": "Which color gets the most engagement on social media?",
        "acceptedAnswer": {
          "@type": "Answer",
          "text": "There is no single best color for all platforms, but research consistently shows that blue performs well on Facebook and Twitter, while warm colors like red and orange tend to generate more saves and shares on Instagram and Pinterest. The key is matching your color choice to both the platform and the emotional response you want to trigger in your audience."
        }
      },
      {
        "@type": "Question",
        "name": "Does color psychology really work across different cultures?",
        "acceptedAnswer": {
          "@type": "Answer",
          "text": "Color psychology has universal elements but also significant cultural variations. For example, white symbolizes purity in Western cultures but is associated with mourning in many East Asian cultures. Red signifies passion or danger in the West but represents prosperity and good fortune in China. If your audience spans multiple cultures, research your primary audience demographics before committing to a color palette."
        }
      },
      {
        "@type": "Question",
        "name": "What colors should I avoid in social media posts?",
        "acceptedAnswer": {
          "@type": "Answer",
          "text": "Muddy, desaturated colors tend to underperform because they lack visual impact in a fast-scrolling feed. Neon or overly saturated colors can feel aggressive and cause viewers to scroll past. The biggest mistake is using colors that clash with your brand identity just because they are trending. Consistency and authenticity in your color choices matter more than chasing trends."
        }
      },
      {
        "@type": "Question",
        "name": "How do I choose a consistent color palette for my social media?",
        "acceptedAnswer": {
          "@type": "Answer",
          "text": "Start by selecting one primary color that reflects your brand personality, then add one or two complementary accent colors. Use tools like Adobe Color or Coolors to find harmonious combinations. Apply your palette consistently across profile photos, post backgrounds, text overlays, and story templates. Document your hex codes and stick with them. Consistency builds recognition, and recognition builds trust with your audience."
        }
      }
    ]
  }
